title: Minimum Deletions to Make String K-Special
summary: Given a string and an integer k, determine the least number of deletions required to ensure that the frequency difference between any two characters in the string does not exceed k.
statement: Given a string and an integer k, determine the least number of deletions required to ensure that the frequency difference between any two characters in the string does not exceed k.
constraints: word is a nonempty lowercase string and k is nonnegative.
After deletions, the frequencies of any two characters still present may differ by at most k.
Return the minimum number of deleted characters; deleting every occurrence removes that character from comparison.
hints: In an optimal nonempty frequency band, its lower bound can be chosen from zero through the word length.
For each candidate minimum v, delete entire smaller groups and trim larger groups to v+k.
Cost(v)=sum(count when count<v; count-v-k when count>v+k); minimize over v.
For fixed v these deletions are individually necessary and sufficient, and every feasible final set has some minimum frequency represented by one candidate.
editorial: For fixed v these deletions are individually necessary and sufficient, and every feasible final set has some minimum frequency represented by one candidate.

tests.explanation: The frequencies are a=4, b=2, c=1; deleting one c and one a twice can leave a and b both twice, requiring three deletions.
Keeping frequencies within a two-count band requires two deletions.
